messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] time heterogeneity for bipartite networks
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

in the latest Siena4 manual (August 20th) at page 46, it's mentioned that
time heterogeneous parameters can be currently implemented only for one-mode
network data.

Is the sienaTimeTest function not suitable for two-mode data either?  Is
there any other way to include time dummies for two mode data at the moment?

Thanks a lot,

Marco

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] problems with little variation in behavioral dependent variable
messages.subject_clean: [Rsiena-help] problems with little variation in behavioral dependent variable
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I try to run a three-waves RSiena analysis with a behavioral dependent variable. After specifying all networks, covariates and behavior files, I try to create the list with effects of the dependent variables with the command "getEffects()". However, this is the error I get:
> paras<-getEffects(project1)
Error in if (val > 0.9) val <- 0.5 : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

I noticed that there is very little variation over time in the behavior variable. When I add a little more variation in the behavior variable, SIENA does read the file without an error.
I expected SIENA to have problems in the analysis given little variation in the behavior. However, I did not expect that it already has problems reading the files in. Does anybody know what to do?

Thanks in advance,
Tobias

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] multigroup analysis with two or more dyadic covariates
messages.subject_clean: [Rsiena-help] multigroup analysis with two or more dyadic covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to run a multigroup analysis which involves main effects of 
several (time-constant) dyadic covariates. The siena07 function crashes 
as soon as I include the main effect of a second (not of the first!) 
dyadic covariate. The error report I get is this:

Error in initializeFRAN(z, x, data, effects, prevAns, initC, profileData 
= profileData,  :
   Dyadic covariate variable 'ADMpath' expected.

In this, "ADMpath" is the name of the second dyadic covariate. When 
running the group-specific projects separately, the error does NOT occur.

Greetings,
Christian

messages.subject_clean: [Rsiena-help] Windows: binaries for RSiena and RSienaTest on CRAN extras
messages.body_plain:
I have put Windows binaries for RSiena and RSienaTest on CRAN extras as 
the builds are failing on R-forge.

This should fix various bugs: problems with multiple processors, behavior 
variables with little variation, multiple groups with dyadic 
covariates, missing distance two effects for behavior variables.

Regards,

Ruth
